title: Idea event
description: One line of _data/ideas.jsonl. Ideas are an append-only event log, not entities: a line is an event that happened, and nothing is ever edited or removed. Current state is folded by replaying events in order, which is what makes the state of any idea at any past moment reconstructible. The legal status transitions are stated here and nowhere else — tools/append_idea.py reads them from this file rather than restating them, so the writer, the projection and the enforcement test cannot drift apart. An idea's ARCH-005 classification is a `classified` event rather than fields on `created`, so the existing corpus is classified by appending, never by rewriting (ADR-024). Rules needing history rather than a single line — that an idea is revisited at most once, and that a second discard is permanent — are enforced by the writer, because a schema validates one event without seeing the ones before it.

idea.description: Six-digit identifier, assigned by tools/append_idea.py and never reused. Shared by every event about the same idea.

event.description: created=the idea was captured | status=its status moved | revisited=a discarded idea was reopened, returning it to reviewing | amended=a prior event's field was corrected without rewriting it | annotated=a note, finding, assessment or lineage was added, permitted on terminal ideas | linked=a typed relationship to another idea or a governed document was asserted | classified=the idea's ARCH-005 record kind and axis values were assigned; the latest one wins

at.description: When the event happened, RFC 3339 with a mandatory offset — a naked local time cannot be ordered against one written in another zone, and ordering is the whole point of the log. The pattern carries the enforcement rather than the format keyword: jsonschema only checks date-time when rfc3339-validator is installed, and it is not a dependency here (see phase-rel-11). The format keyword stays as the declaration of intent and starts enforcing the moment that phase lands. Generated by the writer from the real clock; there is deliberately no way to supply one.

title.description: On `created`, a one-line summary, recorded as given and never edited — an append-only log has no correction path. On `amended`, the replace/inherit shape for this field instead (see `field_shape`); title can never be cleared, because every idea must have one.

body.description: On `created`, the idea in full, as captured, never deduplicated, merged or judged at entry (ADR-010). On `amended`, the replace/inherit shape for this field instead; body can never be cleared, for the same reason as title.

promoted_to.description: What the idea became — one or more governed document codes, named by id. Required when moving to promoted, because a state that does not say what it produced cannot be audited. Newly written promotions are a non-empty array, so one idea can name several documents; the scalar form on the 19 events written before this was an array is read as a singleton, without rewriting them (phase-idea-08).

closes_with.description: Where the delivery happened, required when moving to delivered, resolved or absorbed and forbidden on every other transition. A terminal state with no reference is an assertion; the pointer is what makes the log auditable later (GOV-003, 2026-09-22). Each item names its own kind, so a document code, a phase id and a commit hash are distinguishable without parsing the value. The writer also refuses a pointer that does not resolve.

eid.description: Explicit event identity, generated by the writer for every newly appended event. An amendment names its target by this identity rather than by position, so the pointer survives a rebase or a merge that interleaves two branches' appended lines. Absent on the 19 events written before this field existed; src.db.ideas.identity() falls back to a digest of the event's own bytes for those, so every event has a resolvable identity whether or not it carries one.

amends.description: The identity (see `eid`) of the event this amendment corrects. Must name an event on the same idea that appears earlier in the log; the writer refuses an absent, forward or foreign target before appending, and the fold refuses one on import.

author.description: Who wrote this annotation or classification: `repository-owner` or an agent name. On an annotation, the writer restricts a non-owner author to `kind: finding`, so the owner's own voice in the log stays unambiguous. On a classification, it is the provenance, with the event's `at`: who classified, and when.

kind.description: note=the owner thinking aloud | finding=what a triage agent writes | assessment=a judgement, itself correctable by a later assessment without either being deleted | lineage=how the owner arrived at this idea, such as the compound idea it was pulled out of; structurally inert, never a link (ARCH-005, 000064). An unknown kind fails validation rather than being accepted as free text.

text.description: On `annotated`, the contribution itself. On `amended`, the replace/inherit shape correcting it (see `field_shape`); like title and body, an annotation's text can never be cleared — a textless annotation is not a thing. Annotations accumulate: correcting one never touches the others.

type.description: extends=this idea builds on the target | supersedes=this idea replaces the target (does not discard it — that is a separate, explicit status event) | relates_to=a symmetric relationship, reciprocal by construction | component_of=this atomic idea functions within the target compound idea, many-to-many by design (ARCH-005). Only extends and relates_to may point at a governed document through `target_code`. Each edge is stored once, on the idea that asserts it; the inverse is derived at fold time and never stored, so the two halves cannot disagree.

target.description: On `linked`, the idea this edge points to. On `amended`, the only legal correction is retraction (see `link_retraction`) — a link never mutates its target; there is no shape that repoints one.

target_code.description: On `linked`, the governed document code this edge points to, in place of `target`: a separate field, so a document target and an idea target are distinguishable without parsing the value (REQ-014 R04). The writer refuses a code the governance document registry does not hold. On `amended`, the only legal correction is retraction, as for `target`.

record_kind.description: ARCH-005's record kind, decided before any axis. knowledge=states, asks for, or records something about the domain | collection=exists to group other records | fixture=test or rehearsal data | reference=a pointer to an external source with no claim or ask of its own. Only a knowledge record carries axis values.

ontological.description: ARCH-005 axis 1, the record's subject. concept=Concept / Mental Model | artifact=Artifact / Entity | process=Process / Workflow | event=Event | actor=Actor / Agent | metric=Metric / Standard.

epistemic.description: ARCH-005 axis 2, the truth status of what the record asserts. axiom=Axiom / Ground Truth | hypothesis=Hypothesis / Assumption | anti_pattern=Anti-Pattern / Falsified Concept | not_applicable=Not Applicable / Agnostic, for a record that asserts no verifiable claim; never a stand-in for an unexamined record.

lifecycle.description: ARCH-005 axis 3. generative_seed=Generative Seed | strategic_directive=Strategic Directive | operational_task=Operational Task | retrospective_insight=Retrospective Insight | active=Active / Evergreen | deprecated=Deprecated / Archived, describing the record's subject, never the idea record's own disposition.

temporal.description: ARCH-005 axis 4. as_of=true of a point or interval | standing=true or relevant without a time bound.

lifecycle_remedy.description: How a retrospective_insight could be split: operational_task when the record names one concrete fix, generative_seed when the remedy is left open. Required when lifecycle is retrospective_insight and forbidden otherwise.

decompose.description: True when a knowledge record bundles several unrelated findings of its own (ARCH-005 O6). It is still classified as one record; the flag marks it for the decomposition procedure. Absent reads as false.

reasons.description: Why each value was chosen, keyed by field. A knowledge record carries one for each of the four axes; a reason for the record kind is optional.

confidence.description: How sure the classifier is of each value, 0 to 1, keyed by field like `reasons`. A knowledge record carries one for each of the four axes.

tie_breaks.description: The ARCH-005 tie-break rules the classifier applied, by rule id. Empty or absent when no rule was needed.

status.description: open=captured, nothing has looked at it | triaged=scouting finished, awaiting the owner | reviewing=the owner is actively considering it | promoted=became a plan, requirement or phase; in flight, not finished, and reaches delivered when that work ships | discarded=rejected, terminal unless revisited once | delivered=a working capability exists and was verified, terminal | resolved=the ask was satisfied without building anything, terminal | absorbed=the substance was folded into another document that now carries it, terminal (GOV-003, 2026-09-22)

pointer.description: One place a delivery happened: exactly one of a governed document code, a backlog phase id or a commit hash, keyed by which it is.

document_code.description: A governed document code in either grammar src/governance/codes.py parses: a counter code such as PLAN-029 or PLAN-017.03, or a dated one.

set.description: true=replace this field with `value` | false=inherit whatever the chain already holds

value.description: The replacement. Required when `set` is true, forbidden otherwise. Restricted to a non-empty string here because title, body and text are all required on whatever they belong to and can never be cleared; a future optional, clearable field takes a wider `value` type in its own right rather than loosening this one (see `link_retraction` for exactly that field).

link_retraction.description: The only legal amendment to a link's target: `set` is always true and `value` is always null. This is what 'clear' means for the one contribution PLAN-017.04 permits retracting rather than correcting — there is deliberately no shape that replaces one target with another, because a link never mutates what it points to.

allOf.description: A created event carries the prose and nothing about status; the idea begins open by definition, so an explicit transition into it would be a second way to say the same thing.

Status transitions move forward only. discarded is reachable from every working state but is never a from — the one way out of it is a revisited event, which is what limits reopening to once. delivered, resolved and absorbed are reachable from every working state and are never a from. promoted is not terminal: its one way on is to delivered, when the work it became ships (GOV-003, 2026-09-22). A move to delivered, resolved or absorbed requires closes_with, as promoted requires promoted_to; no other transition carries one.
A revisit is an attribute of an idea's history, not a status. It returns a discarded idea to reviewing and carries no prose; an idea worth revisiting twice is a new idea, recorded separately.

An amendment corrects a prior event's field without rewriting it — nothing in an append-only log can be rewritten, so a correction is a new line naming what it changes. It carries only the fields it corrects, each as a field_shape (or, for a link's target, the narrower link_retraction), and never the raw status, annotation or link vocabulary those events own.

An annotation adds a note, finding or assessment without moving status — permitted on every idea, including a terminal one, because it corrects or extends the record rather than the state machine. Annotations accumulate; they are never replaced, only individually corrected by a later amendment naming this event's identity.

A link asserts a typed, one-directional edge to another idea, or, for extends and relates_to only, to a governed document through target_code — exactly one of the two. Its inverse is derived at fold time and never stored, so the two halves cannot disagree. A link never mutates anything once written — its only legal amendment is the retraction in link_retraction, and even that leaves this line exactly as written.
A pointer belongs to a status event; which transitions require one is stated in the status branch.
A document target belongs to a link, or to the amendment retracting one.
Classification fields belong to a classified event and to nothing else.

A classification (ARCH-005, ADR-024) names who classified and the record kind. A knowledge record carries one value, a reason and a confidence on each of the four axes, with no axis blank; a collection, fixture or reference record carries none of them. lifecycle_remedy appears exactly when lifecycle is retrospective_insight. A later classified event replaces an earlier one in the fold; neither is edited.
